narration.text: In this video, we'll build an interactive dashboard from a file of U.S. flight data, using Claude Code in a GitHub codespace. We won't write any code ourselves.

steps.notes: Episode frame (R30). Motion graphics on screen (R69): text slides over a still of the finished dashboard, rendered in Remotion; see remotion/ OpeningRecap. The take itself starts at p1.01.

narration.text: Claude Code can discover the data, propose options, and build the whole solution. That's powerful, but it's also easy to get a result you didn't want if you don't know how to direct it.

This exercise uses a direction prompt. A direction prompt describes the goal, the audience, and the quality you expect, and leaves the technical decisions to the AI. It's how a manager gives direction to an analyst.

A construction prompt is the opposite. It spells out exactly what to build, such as a bar chart of flights by region, using matplotlib. Use a construction prompt when you know exactly what you want. Use a direction prompt when you know the goal, but not the path.

We'll work through the exercise in order. First, we'll find the data and open Claude Code. Then we'll ask for the dashboard, choose from Claude's options, and let it build. Finally, we'll explore the dashboard, request a fix, and save our work to GitHub.

narration.text: Let's recap. We found the flight data and opened Claude Code. We gave Claude two standing rules and a direction prompt, chose Plotly Dash from its options, and let it build. We explored the dashboard and asked Claude to fix a problem only we could see. And we saved our work to GitHub.

ide.notes: Off camera, before OBS starts: VS Code saves open editors and folder expansion in the codespace, so the previous take's state (data expanded, the CSV open) is reset first. The Claude Code panel reopens its last session, so prepare clicks New session (and returns to Chat).

generated.defect: After I click Last 24 mo, the two boxes at the ends of the date slider read 45 and 68 (month numbers) where I expected dates such as Oct 2023 and Sep 2025.
generated.notes: Explored off camera on full_take02's dashboard (explore/: inventory, try_01..07). The map and the ranking sit below the first screen (page 2697 px), so every interaction is in the first screen: the Last 24 mo preset (a filter), the Metric dropdown to Cancellation rate (a parameter, two clicks), the Airport focus dropdown to ABQ Albuquerque (the drill-in, two clicks; its label names the map, bar, dot and watchlist clicks). The defect meets R70's four tests: (1) visible at once, the boxes sit at the top left; (2) one sentence: clicked Last 24 mo, saw 45 and 68, expected dates; (3) one round: Dash 4.4's RangeSlider draws these number boxes, which can be hidden or replaced; (4) shown fixed by clicking Last 24 mo again after the reload. The doc's map example does not occur (the map doesn't zoom on a focus). The defect test is by class (.dash-range-slider-input), not the slider's id, so a rebuilt slider can't stop the take by accident. Claude's build reply says it never saw the page in a browser (no browser in the codespace), which p5.15a's line rests on. Another visible flaw, not chosen: the trend's end labels overlap at the right edge (small, and hard to test after a fix).
